title: JavaScript secret and retired-library disclosure
summary: Mine first-party JS bundles for exposed secrets and client-reconstructed signing keys, and flag retired/vulnerable library versions. An unverified string is a low lead; a verified live credential or a public HMAC reconstruction is the finding.
steps: fetch_lazy_chunks (dry_run then download) on a first-party webpack/Vite/Next/Angular runtime; extract_js_endpoints and ingest in-scope paths. 404s on hash-map ids are expected.
scan_js_urls_for_secrets / execute_gitleaks / execute_hermes on the bundles (…/_next/static/chunks/*.js, main-es2015.*.js, main.*.js). Bundles are often 5-10MB; do not skip them.

Hostname-keyed objects mapping prod/dev/qa to client_id + client_secret, Sentry DSNs, and MuleSoft/API credentials are leads; env-config objects (client encryption_key, EmailJS ids) are filed as separate findings.
CWE-321 client HMAC: a secret reconstructed via Object.keys(obj).join('') or for-in concat and fed to HmacSHA256 / HS256 JWT signing is SUBMIT on presence — the literal never appears.

Verify a live OAuth/API secret with ONE in-scope read-only call (result count + 1-2 redacted fields); prefer sandbox/dev. Do not bulk-export. HMAC/ICS secrets are the finding on public reconstruction.
Flag retired or known-vulnerable library versions (retire.js-style) as a separate hardening lead, not a secret.
sanitize_evidence before submit; rotate every exposed pair in remediation and recommend a server-side proxy. queue_finding_followups(vuln_type='js_secrets').
pass_signals: A live credential or a client-reconstructed signing key from a public bundle
A hostname-keyed client_id/client_secret or a Sentry/MuleSoft secret confirmed
kill_signals: The value is a public, non-sensitive configuration key
